title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is seeing a mix of capital raises and strategic partnerships, with a focus on satellite technology and defense applications. Meanwhile, budgetary concerns loom large as the defense sector grapples with funding uncertainties.

themes.title: Capital Raises and Investments
themes.body: Creotech's $118 million capital raise for a new satellite factory signals a growing appetite for production capabilities. Similarly, Cowboy's $275 million round emphasizes the trend of integrating orbital data with launch systems.

themes.title: Defense Budget Woes
themes.body: The failure to pass a defense budget could hinder the U.S. space race, potentially stalling critical programs. The recent $1.4 billion addition to the space resilience line may not be enough to offset these concerns.

themes.title: Partnerships in Space Tech
themes.body: Anduril and L3Harris's collaboration on a tactical SDA constellation bid highlights the increasing importance of joint ventures in space technology. Such alliances are becoming essential for navigating the complex landscape of defense needs.

themes.title: Shifting Focus on AI and Data
themes.body: The rise of AI applications in defense, as evidenced by the growing interest from YC companies, reflects a pivotal shift in how data is leveraged in military contexts. Operational AI's limitations in Earth observation data further underscore the challenges ahead.
